title: OSHA general industry permit-required confined spaces practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry permit-required confined spaces practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.146. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule.

questions.question: Under 1910.146(a), which type of employment is outside the scope of the permit-required confined spaces section?

options.A: Warehouse employment
options.B: Construction
options.C: Food processing employment
options.D: Chemical plant employment

questions.explanation: The section "does not apply to agriculture, to construction, or to shipyard employment".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: This section does not apply to agriculture, to construction, or to shipyard employment (parts 1928, 1926, and 1915 of this chapter, respectively).

questions.question: Which of these is one of the three elements in the 1910.146(b) definition of a confined space?

options.A: It is at least 5 feet deep
options.B: It contains a hazardous atmosphere
options.C: It has a single opening less than 24 inches across
options.D: It is not designed for continuous employee occupancy

questions.explanation: A confined space, among its three elements, "Is not designed for continuous employee occupancy."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (3) Is not designed for continuous employee occupancy.

questions.question: How many of the listed characteristics must a confined space have to be a permit-required confined space under 1910.146(b)?

options.A: One or more
options.B: At least two
options.C: At least three
options.D: All four

questions.explanation: A permit space is a confined space "that has one or more of the following characteristics".

questions.question: What level of flammable gas, vapor, or mist does the 1910.146(b) definition of hazardous atmosphere set?

options.A: In excess of 50 percent of its lower flammable limit
options.B: In excess of 25 percent of its lower flammable limit
options.C: In excess of 10 percent of its lower flammable limit
options.D: In excess of 100 percent of its lower flammable limit

questions.explanation: The first listed cause is "Flammable gas, vapor, or mist in excess of 10 percent of its lower flammable limit (LFL)".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which oxygen concentrations does the 1910.146(b) definition of hazardous atmosphere list as a cause?

options.A: Below 16 percent or above 25 percent
options.B: Below 19.5 percent or above 23.5 percent
options.C: Below 18 percent or above 22 percent
options.D: Below 20.9 percent or above 21.5 percent

questions.explanation: The definition lists "Atmospheric oxygen concentration below 19.5 percent or above 23.5 percent".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (3) Atmospheric oxygen concentration below 19.5 percent or above 23.5 percent;

questions.question: Under the 1910.146(b) definition of entry, when is entry considered to have occurred?

options.A: As soon as any part of the entrant's body breaks the plane of an opening into the space
options.B: When the entrant's whole body is inside the space
options.C: When the entrant's head passes through the opening
options.D: When the entrant begins the assigned work inside the space

questions.explanation: Entry "is considered to have occurred as soon as any part of the entrant's body breaks the plane of an opening into the space."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Entry includes ensuing work activities in that space and is considered to have occurred as soon as any part of the entrant's body breaks the plane of an opening into the space.

questions.topic: Workplace evaluation, warning signs and contractors
questions.question: If the workplace contains permit spaces, how does 1910.146(c)(2) require the employer to inform exposed employees of them?

options.A: Only by a verbal briefing when each employee is hired
options.B: By listing the spaces on the OSHA injury and illness log
options.C: Only by a written notice mailed to each employee's home
options.D: By posting danger signs or by any other equally effective means

questions.explanation: The employer must inform exposed employees "by posting danger signs or by any other equally effective means" of the existence, location and danger of the permit spaces.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the workplace contains permit spaces, the employer shall inform exposed employees, by posting danger signs or by any other equally effective means, of the existence and location of and the danger posed by the permit spaces.

questions.topic: Workplace evaluation, warning signs and contractors
questions.question: What does 1910.146(c)(3) require of an employer that decides its employees will not enter permit spaces?

options.A: Nothing further, because the section no longer applies to it
options.B: Only a written notice to OSHA that no entries will take place
options.C: Effective measures to prevent its employees from entering the permit spaces
options.D: Entry permits for each permit space every day

questions.explanation: That employer "shall take effective measures to prevent its employees from entering the permit spaces" and must still comply with paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(6) and (c)(8).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the employer decides that its employees will not enter permit spaces, the employer shall take effective measures to prevent its employees from entering the permit spaces and shall comply with paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(6), and (c)(8) of this section.

questions.question: To use the alternate procedures in 1910.146(c)(5), the employer must be able to demonstrate that the only hazard posed by the permit space is which one?

options.A: A material that could engulf an entrant
options.B: An actual or potential hazardous atmosphere
options.C: Inwardly converging walls
options.D: Moving machinery inside the space

questions.explanation: The employer must demonstrate "that the only hazard posed by the permit space is an actual or potential hazardous atmosphere".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (A) The employer can demonstrate that the only hazard posed by the permit space is an actual or potential hazardous atmosphere;

questions.question: Under the alternate procedures in 1910.146(c)(5)(ii)(C), in what order must the internal atmosphere be tested before an employee enters?

options.A: Oxygen content, then flammable gases and vapors, then potential toxic air contaminants
options.B: Potential toxic air contaminants, then flammable gases and vapors, then oxygen content
options.C: Flammable gases and vapors, then oxygen content, then potential toxic air contaminants
options.D: Flammable gases and vapors, then potential toxic air contaminants, then oxygen content

questions.explanation: The atmosphere must be tested with a calibrated direct-reading instrument "for oxygen content, for flammable gases and vapors, and for potential toxic air contaminants, in that order."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Before an employee enters the space, the internal atmosphere shall be tested, with a calibrated direct-reading instrument, for oxygen content, for flammable gases and vapors, and for potential toxic air contaminants, in that order.

questions.question: Under 1910.146(d)(4), on what cost basis must the employer provide equipment such as testing, ventilating, lighting and rescue equipment?

options.A: Employees pay for half of the cost
options.B: Employees pay for their own personal protective equipment only
options.C: Employees pay unless the equipment is reused
options.D: At no cost to employees

questions.explanation: The employer must provide the listed equipment "at no cost to employees, maintain that equipment properly, and ensure that employees use that equipment properly".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Provide the following equipment (specified in paragraphs (d)(4)(i) through (d)(4)(ix) of this section) at no cost to employees, maintain that equipment properly, and ensure that employees use that equipment properly:

questions.question: What does the note to 1910.146(c)(7) say about controlling atmospheric hazards through forced air ventilation?

options.A: It counts as elimination once it has run for one hour
options.B: It counts as elimination when the entry supervisor certifies it
options.C: It does not constitute elimination of the hazards
options.D: It allows reclassification for the rest of the shift

questions.explanation: The note states: "Control of atmospheric hazards through forced air ventilation does not constitute elimination of the hazards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Note: Control of atmospheric hazards through forced air ventilation does not constitute elimination of the hazards.

questions.question: Under 1910.146(c)(7)(iv), what must each employee do if hazards arise within a permit space that has been declassified to a non-permit space?

options.A: Exit the space
options.B: Finish the current task and then report the hazard
options.C: Put on a respirator and continue working
options.D: Keep working while the attendant tests the atmosphere

questions.explanation: If hazards arise in a declassified space, "each employee in the space shall exit the space", and the employer then reevaluates it.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If hazards arise within a permit space that has been declassified to a non-permit space under paragraph (c)(7) of this section, each employee in the space shall exit the space.

questions.topic: Workplace evaluation, warning signs and contractors
questions.question: When does 1910.146(c)(8)(v) require the host employer to debrief the contractor?

options.A: Only if someone is injured during entry
options.B: At the conclusion of the entry operations
options.C: Once a year at the program review
options.D: Before the contractor is hired

questions.explanation: The host employer must "Debrief the contractor at the conclusion of the entry operations" on the program followed and any hazards confronted or created.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (v) Debrief the contractor at the conclusion of the entry operations regarding the permit space program followed and regarding any hazards confronted or created in permit spaces during entry operations.

questions.question: What minimum retention period does 1910.146(e)(6) set for each canceled entry permit?

options.A: At least 30 days
options.B: At least 90 days
options.C: At least 6 months
options.D: At least 1 year

questions.explanation: The employer "shall retain each canceled entry permit for at least 1 year" to support the program review.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall retain each canceled entry permit for at least 1 year to facilitate the review of the permit-required confined space program required by paragraph (d)(14) of this section.

questions.question: What limit does 1910.146(e)(4) set on the duration of an entry permit?

options.A: 8 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: The time required to complete the assigned task or job identified on the permit
options.D: One calendar week

questions.explanation: "The duration of the permit may not exceed the time required to complete the assigned task or job identified on the permit".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The duration of the permit may not exceed the time required to complete the assigned task or job identified on the permit in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section.

questions.question: Under 1910.146(e)(5), which event requires the entry supervisor to terminate entry and cancel the entry permit?

options.A: A condition that is not allowed under the entry permit arises in or near the permit space
options.B: An authorized entrant takes a scheduled break
options.C: A new attendant takes over at a shift change
options.D: The permit is posted at the entry portal

questions.explanation: The entry supervisor must terminate entry and cancel the permit when entry operations are completed or when "A condition that is not allowed under the entry permit arises in or near the permit space."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (ii) A condition that is not allowed under the entry permit arises in or near the permit space.

questions.topic: Training and duties of entry roles
questions.question: What must the training certification required by 1910.146(g)(4) contain?

options.A: Only the name of the training company
options.B: The trainer's license number and the course price
options.C: The employee's home address and date of birth
options.D: Each employee's name, the signatures or initials of the trainers, and the dates of training

questions.explanation: "The certification shall contain each employee's name, the signatures or initials of the trainers, and the dates of training."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The certification shall contain each employee's name, the signatures or initials of the trainers, and the dates of training.

questions.question: Under 1910.146(i)(4), how long must the attendant remain outside the permit space during entry operations?

options.A: Until the first hour of entry has passed
options.B: Until relieved by another attendant
options.C: Until the entrants have started their work
options.D: Until the entry supervisor arrives

questions.explanation: Each attendant "Remains outside the permit space during entry operations until relieved by another attendant".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (4) Remains outside the permit space during entry operations until relieved by another attendant;

questions.topic: Rescue, emergency services and employee participation
questions.question: What is the longest interval 1910.146(k)(2)(iv) allows between practice permit space rescues by employees designated to provide rescue?

options.A: 18 months
options.B: 24 months
options.C: 12 months
options.D: 36 months

questions.explanation: Affected employees must "practice making permit space rescues at least once every 12 months" through simulated rescue operations.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Ensure that affected employees practice making permit space rescues at least once every 12 months, by means of simulated rescue operations in which they remove dummies, manikins, or actual persons from the actual permit spaces or from representative permit spaces.
